title: OpenLiDARViewer validation dataset register
description: Shape of validation/datasets/dataset-register.yaml. A dataset record is what a later cross-implementation run or field study cites INSTEAD of prose, so every field a reader would otherwise have to guess is required here. The semantic rules that this schema cannot express (unit/axis agreement, checkpoint independence, checksum drift) live in scripts/verify-dataset-register.mjs and are enforced by the same command.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped only when a field is added, removed, or re-typed. A consumer that does not know the version must refuse the file rather than read it partially.

sentinelOrNumber.description: A measured number, or one of two sentinels. `not-applicable` means the quantity has no meaning for this dataset (point density of a raster). `unknown` means it has meaning and was not measured. They are kept apart because a verifier can demand a number for the second case and never for the first.

datasetId.description: The citation handle. Stable for the life of the register: a study that cited it must keep resolving, so a record is superseded by adding a new id, never by editing an old one.

sourceUrl.description: Where the bytes came from: an http(s) URL for external data, or a repo-relative path for data this repository generates. An http(s) URL without an immutable marker is treated as mutable and must carry a checksum.

landingPage.description: The human-readable page or README that states the licence and provenance. Separate from sourceUrl because the licence usually is not served with the bytes.

licence.description: SPDX identifier where one exists, otherwise the licence name as the provider writes it. `unknown` is rejected by the verifier: an unlicensed dataset cannot be cited as evidence.

redistribution.description: What this project may do with the bytes, not what the licence says about the world in general.

acquisitionDate.description: When THIS project obtained or generated the bytes. Distinct from captureDate, which is when the sensor flew.

sourceSha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes used. `not-fetched` is legal only for a record whose storage says the bytes were deliberately not retrieved.

captureDate.description: ISO date, an ISO range (`2020-03-01/2022-11-30`) for a multi-season programme, or `not-applicable` for synthetic data.

horizontalCrs.description: EPSG code with its name, or `local-metric-grid` / `local-foot-grid` when the file declares no CRS at all. A blank is rejected: a metric claim without a frame is not checkable.

verticalCrs.description: The vertical datum, stated separately. An ellipsoidal height and an orthometric height differ by tens of metres, and a register that merged the two axes would hide that.

horizontalUnits.description: `not-applicable` is legal only when horizontalCrs also says not-applicable. The verifier enforces the pairing, so the sentinel cannot be used to slip past the unit/axis check.

verticalUnits.description: `not-applicable` for a derived raster whose cell values are not lengths (slope degrees, a shading index). Paired with verticalCrs the same way horizontalUnits is.

nominalDensity.description: Points per square metre as the provider reports it, or a sentinel. Not recomputed here.

terrainClasses.description: Terrain regimes present, so a study can select datasets by difficulty rather than by name.

containsIndependentCheckpoints.description: True only when the dataset ships survey checkpoints that were withheld from every processing step. Adjusted control is not a checkpoint.

checkpointSource.description: Who measured the checkpoints and how. `not-applicable` when there are none. Must not name this project: a checkpoint produced by the software under test measures nothing.

knownLimitations.description: What this dataset cannot settle. Written before any run, so a later result cannot quietly widen the dataset's reach.

storage.description: Whether the bytes are in this repository (`committed`), held outside it by whoever ran the study (`acquired`), or deliberately not retrieved because access is restricted (`restricted`). See the header comment in dataset-register.yaml for why this field has to exist.

localPath.description: Repo-relative path to the committed bytes. Required when storage is `committed`, and the only way a verifier can recompute a checksum instead of trusting the recorded one.

controlPointIds.description: Points consumed by processing (boresight, strip adjustment, datum fit). Needed as an explicit list because the reuse of a control point as a checkpoint is invisible when only counts are recorded.

checkpointIds.description: Points withheld from processing and used only to measure error. Must not intersect controlPointIds.

evidenceRole.description: What agreement with this dataset can prove, independent of what the bytes are. `fixture`: synthetic/unit input, exercises code paths not accuracy. `oracle`: cross-implementation reference (GDAL, PDAL, libE57, etc.), agreement catches coding errors not truth. `checkpoint-source`: independent survey truth withheld from processing. `reference-labelling`: a producer's own classification used as a reference, not as ground truth. `sample-scene`: a real cloud used for exploratory agreement, no accuracy claim on its own.
